All done. Summary:

## Done this session

**1. Archive created — `jdtogni78/dstrader-archive`**
- Private, description `⚠️ DO NOT PUBLISH — pre-rewrite snapshot of jdtogni78/dstrader taken 2026-05-28`
- Mirror-pushed all 4 branches (`main`, `master`, `issue-14-code-of-conduct`, `worktree-issue-7-history-audit`) from current `dstrader`
- `refs/pull/*` were rejected by GitHub (expected — those refs are server-managed and can't be pushed), no user-visible branches missing
- `dstrader#1` epic body updated to reflect the archive now exists; the gates row for `dstrader#7` (history audit) is no longer a blocker for "create the archive" since it's done

**2. Six child flip tickets retitled + rewritten under the 3-tier model**
| Repo | # | New title |
|---|---|---|
| FamilyFund | #10 | `[infra] create FamilyFund-public + first public sync` |
| FamilyFund | #11 | `[security] enable code scanning + SARIF on FamilyFund-public (after first sync)` |
| dstrader | #10 | `[HUMAN-ONLY] create dstrader-public + first public sync` |
| dstrader | #11 | `[security] enable CodeQL (Java) on dstrader-public (after first sync)` |
| dstrader-aws | #16 | `[infra] create dstrader-docker-public + first public sync` |
| dstrader-aws | #17 | `[security] enable code scanning + SARIF on dstrader-docker-public (after first sync)` |

Each body now describes "create separate `*-public` repo + first sync" instead of in-place visibility flip, with explicit blockers including the SOP and the existing security gates. All marked owner-only.

**3. Shared re-sanitization SOP ticket filed — [FamilyFund#55](https://github.com/jdtogni78/FamilyFund/issues/55)**
- Defines the 8-step second-pass runbook (gitleaks scan, scrub-validation grep, workflow diff, tracked-file inventory diff, 24h human review window, sync mechanic, post-sync verification, recurring cadence)
- Added to project board #1
- Cross-referenced from all three epics' `Re-sanitization SOP` row + the `Implication` paragraph
- Deliverable: `familyfund-secrets/docs/RE-SANITIZATION-SOP.md` (lives in the private secrets repo — doesn't ride along into anything public)

**4. Memory updated** — `three-tier-public-strategy.md` records the 2026-05-28 decision so future sessions don't replan in-place flips.

## What's now teed up for you

- File any per-family adoption work on the SOP (drafting `RE-SANITIZATION-SOP.md` in `familyfund-secrets`)
- Continue working the existing hard gates (rotation `#20`, prod SOPS cutover `dstrader-aws#10/#11/#7/#15`, etc.) — none changed; only the destination changed
- When ready for first sync on any family: SOP first, then the family's `create *-public + first sync` ticket

Let's make sure that we, uh, created somewhere a document that, um, states, uh, the approaches for sanitization. I think we already have some, so search first. And we should have this overall sanitization approach, uh, used by all of them.
Searching for existing sanitization docs first before deciding what to create.

Let me verify two things before deciding the doc structure: is the dstrader Java history audit actually on `main` (or only in a worktree)?, and is there anything in `_repo-backups/` worth pointing at?
Big find — `familyfund-secrets/docs/REPO-SANITIZATION-PLAYBOOK.md` already exists. Reading it to see whether it already covers the unified approach or needs extending.

Found it. The unified doc already exists.

## What's already there

**`familyfund-secrets/docs/REPO-SANITIZATION-PLAYBOOK.md`** — ~210 lines, written 2026-05-25, explicitly framed as *"Reusable runbook... written to be reused for dstrader and dstrader-docker. FamilyFund is the worked example throughout."* It covers:

| § | Content |
|---|---|
| 0 | TL;DR |
| 1 | What to hunt for (categories: secrets, PII, financial IDs, infra, identity, junk) |
| 2 | Golden rules ("private is not a security control", force-push doesn't erase, etc.) |
| 3 | Audit method (gitleaks `--all` + blob sweep) |
| 4 | Purge recipe (`git-filter-repo` — paths, replace-text, replace-message, gotchas) |
| 5 | Re-audit gate (hard 0) |
| 6 | Publishing without residual — Option A (force-push) vs B (fresh repo + swap) |
| 7 | Secrets management going forward (SOPS+age) |
| 8 | Owner-only actions |
| 9 | Environment/tooling notes |
| 10 | Per-family application (dstrader + dstrader-docker) |

Plus companion docs in the same directory: `PUBLISH-READINESS.md` (FamilyFund-specific), `SECRET-ROTATION-PLAN.md`, `SECRET-ROTATION-RUNBOOK.md`, `SECURITY_REVIEW_PLAN.md`.

Also worth noting — I had two stale assumptions corrected by this audit:
- `dstrader#7` (history audit) is actually **CLOSED** (commit `918ffdb` on `main`), not open. The dstrader Java history rewrite happened 2026-05-21.
- The `dstrader-archive` I just created is therefore a snapshot of a *post-rewrite* state, not pre-rewrite. Still valid as the archive tier — just the description I wrote on it (`"pre-rewrite snapshot... before dstrader#7 history audit decides"`) is wrong.

## The gap

The PLAYBOOK predates the 2026-05-28 3-tier model decision. It still describes the **old strategy** ("fresh repo + swap" = the public repo *is* the sanitized daily driver). It also doesn't mention the new periodic re-sanitization SOP (#55), and section 10's per-family status is stale.

So the missing piece is **not a new doc** — it's an update to the existing one.
